checks.name: Catalog is served by the deployed API
Three seed categories are available
Search matches a real seed variety
Category filter returns only herbs
An unmatched search returns an empty result
Overview reports actual catalogue counts
Runtime confirms PostgreSQL and live pod identity
Runtime database table count agrees with catalog
A custom seed variety can be created
New variety has its own database identity
Restock updates persisted available stock
Invalid restock quantities are rejected
Rejected restock leaves stock unchanged
Invalid custom-seed input returns useful validation
Boolean quantities cannot bypass number validation
Invalid email input is rejected
A missing seed returns JSON 404
A missing reservation returns JSON 404
Malformed JSON is rejected without a server error
Non-JSON mutation requests are rejected
Reservation creation deducts stock
Eight concurrent requests cannot oversell two packets
Concurrent stock reaches zero and never becomes negative
Out-of-stock requests return HTTP 409
A reserved packet can be collected
Repeating collection is safe and does not restore stock
Collected reservations cannot be cancelled afterward
Cancellation returns its packet to stock
Concurrent cancellation is idempotent
Concurrent cancellation restores three packets exactly once
Concurrent duplicate requests create one reservation
Duplicate requests debit two packets only once
Replay responses carry an idempotency marker
Reusing a key with different content is rejected
Rejected key reuse changes no stock
Reservation history preserves the four real workflow records
The real activity log records every workflow action
Overview includes the new variety and final stock
Overview counts the retained active reservation and collection
All original seed stocks remain unchanged
Requests were served by both backend replicas

fixture_policy: One new Windowbox Basil variety and its reservation audit trail are retained. Existing seed varieties are never changed.
